info.title: Agnes Smart Home API
info.description:
Agnes Smart Home API manages device provisioning, MQTT credentials, certificate-based onboarding, shadows, and telemetry visibility for local smart-home hardware.

Primary workflows:
- Register and authenticate an admin user with JWT bearer tokens.
- Provision a device and receive one-time MQTT credentials plus PEM certificate material.
- Generate a time-limited claim code for hotspot onboarding from a Pico subscriber or other field device.
- Exchange that claim code for runtime MQTT credentials and DER certificate bundles.
- Observe device health, message logs, webhook events, and dashboard summaries.
- Read or update device shadow state and manage per-device MQTT policies.

MQTT and onboarding model:
- Local broker listeners typically use port 1883 for username/password clients and port 8883 for mutual TLS clients.
- Claim exchange returns the runtime topic namespace, MQTT broker details, and DER payloads expected by the Pico flows in this repository.
- Certificate renewal revokes the prior client certificate, so stale device bundles should not be reused after a claim or renew operation.

Security model:
- Admin and management endpoints use JWT bearer authentication.
- Integration keys use scoped `X-API-Key` access for scripts, dashboards, and automation systems.
- Recommended integration scopes include presets such as read-only monitoring, device automation, fleet admin, and webhook worker.
- Device heartbeat accepts device Basic auth or API key auth as documented by the endpoint contract.
- In non-local deployments the OpenAPI schema also advertises `X-Api-Key` support for gateway-managed access.

post.summary: Create a hotspot onboarding claim code
post.description: Generate a short-lived claim code that a Pico or other field device can exchange for runtime MQTT credentials and DER certificate material. This flow is intended for physical devices, not browser MQTT clients.

post.summary: Exchange a claim code for runtime device credentials
post.description: Complete field onboarding by exchanging a valid claim code for topic namespace details, MQTT credentials, and DER-encoded certificate assets. The returned DER bundle is for embedded/device MQTT clients; browser dashboards should use Agnes WebSocket realtime or a separate broker WebSocket listener with browser-compatible authentication.

post.description: Register an outbound webhook endpoint for Agnes MQTT and device lifecycle events. Supported events include `mqtt.client.connected`, `mqtt.client.disconnected`, `mqtt.message.published`, `mqtt.command.received`, `mqtt.status.received`, `mqtt.sensor.received`, `mqtt.auth.failed`, `mqtt.subscription.created`, and `mqtt.subscription.removed`. Legacy aliases `connect`, `disconnect`, and `publish` remain accepted.
